evidence.source: 李學勤主編《字源》, 天津古籍出版社／遼寧人民出版社, 2012
evidence.field: PDF p. 658; printed p. 645; 米 entry continuation; scan inspected
evidence.text: The entry describes 米 as a pictograph resembling scattered grains: small marks lie above and below a horizontal stroke, later changing into longer strokes and a cross-like form. It gives the original sense as seeds of grain crops with their husks removed, then notes later broader use for shelled kernels such as 花生米, embroidered patterns resembling grains, and a measure meaning a small amount. The printed page and passage were checked against the supplied scan; the headword 米 is at the bottom of PDF p. 657 (printed p. 644), and the explanation continues at the top of p. 658. No OCR correction was identified in the inspected passage.

evidence.source: Chinese University of Hong Kong, 漢語多功能字庫
evidence.field: 漢字甲骨部件分析 / 形義通解, lines 122–126
evidence.text: The account identifies 米 with grain kernels whose husks have been removed and cites the Zhouli distinction between 米 and 粟. It describes modern 花生米 as an extension to shelled kernels. For the graphic interpretation, it reports small marks above and below a central stroke; Li Xiaoding interprets the stroke as a sieve, while Bai Yuzheng proposes a grain stalk. It also reports oracle-bone uses for grain, 敉 ‘pacify’, and a sacrificial name, and bronze uses as clan names. These are the database’s reports, not independently dated artifact attestations.
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析：米

evidence.source: NTNU Chinese Academic Annual, article discussing 王育《許氏說文解字六書論正》
evidence.text: The article reviews competing explanations of the central stroke, including a sieve proposal and readings of the whole graph as scattered or dehusked grain. It supports a broad early grain referent rather than a single crop, commonly specialized to rice in modern usage. The discussion does not establish precise first-use dates or a complete chronology for that specialization.
evidence.title: 中國學術年刊第四十七期（春季號）

evidence.field: 字形解說 and 字音及字義, lines 11–22
evidence.text: This account describes oracle-bone 米 as scattered grains around a central horizontal stroke, which it interprets as spacing in a rack for placing rice; it says the middle develops into a 十 shape in small seal script. It gives the basic sense as grain after husking, specifically rice in a narrower use. This is a distinct proposed explanation for the central stroke; the scan-verified 字源 and CUHK accounts record other proposals.
